encoder: Sonnet 5.5, a single agent working alone from BRIEF.md (no subagents)
display_name: Terrorism Act 2000, Part III (Terrorist Property): whole encoding with a seat layer, main dialect
seat: a person who handles, funds or deals in money or other property that may be terrorist property, asking on facts they can state whether they commit an offence under Part III or have a defence, and what they must disclose to whom and when

scope.encoded: Part III of the Terrorism Act 2000 (United Kingdom), sections 14 to 23B, as deposited: the whole of the text, every section, subsection, paragraph and defined term having a row in the coverage table in NOTES.md
scope.not_encoded: sections 24 to 31, which are shown repealed in the text (coverage rows only); Schedule 3A, the Banking and Financial Dealings Act 1971, the standard scale, the definitions of terrorism and proscribed organisation, the 2017 Regulations and Schedule 4, which are not among the sources and are asked as inputs
scope.edition: legislation.gov.uk, latest revised version of Part III, point in time 2026-07-08, retrieved 2026-11-05; a converter rendering, not the official text

not_reviewed: No domain expert has read this encoding against the text. It was written and checked by one Sonnet 5.5 agent from a converter rendering, not the official text, and has not been reviewed by a lawyer. The readings listed under 'Marginal readings for a lawyer' in NOTES.md are the brief's status quo, not rulings.

checks.tool: check.sh with L4=<l4 1.6.109> L4_MAIN=<l4 1.6.108>, target main, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.srcrefs: python3 -I srcrefs.py check --refs ukpga-2000-11-part-3.txt ta-*.l4 reports 0 problems

dependencies.instrument: Terrorism Act 2000, Schedule 3A (what a business in the regulated sector, a credit institution, a financial institution and a supervisory authority are)
dependencies.taken_as_input: whether the information came in the course of a business in the regulated sector, and whether a person is a credit institution, a financial institution or a supervisory authority, each stated as a fact; in the seat, the regulated-sector fact in the question about what to tell and to whom can be answered "I am not sure", which is NOTHING

dependencies.instrument: Terrorism Act 2000, Parts I and II (the meaning of "terrorism" and of "proscribed organisation")
dependencies.taken_as_input: whether property is likely to be used for the purposes of terrorism, is the proceeds of acts of terrorism, or belongs to a proscribed organisation, each stated as a fact

dependencies.instrument: Banking and Financial Dealings Act 1971 (bank holidays) and the date of Good Friday
dependencies.taken_as_input: one list of dates, asked of the person (Saturdays, Sundays and Christmas Day are computed from the calendar)

dependencies.instrument: The statutory maximum and level 5 on the standard scale (amounts of fines)
dependencies.taken_as_input: the amount of the fine, as a number the person states; penalties are always ceilings
whether two institutions belong to the same group, stated as a fact
whether a country or territory imposes equivalent money laundering requirements, stated as a fact

dependencies.instrument: The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 (who is a person's supervisory authority)
dependencies.taken_as_input: whether the disclosure is to the authority that is the person's supervisory authority, stated as a fact

dependencies.instrument: Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 (section 412, legal privilege in Scotland; investigations and court orders under that Act; section 339ZL, a combined code of practice)
dependencies.taken_as_input: whether the information would be privileged, and whether a disclosure is for an investigation or order under that Act, each stated as a fact

dependencies.instrument: Crime and Courts Act 2013, section 1(5) (the criminal intelligence function)
dependencies.taken_as_input: whether the provision of information is for the purposes of the criminal intelligence function, stated as a fact

dependencies.instrument: Counter-Terrorism Act 2008, sections 30, 31 and 94, and the Sentencing Code, section 69 (ancillary offences; a terrorist connection)
dependencies.taken_as_input: whether an offence is an ancillary offence, and whether a court has determined or proved that an offence has a terrorist connection, each stated as a fact

dependencies.instrument: Terrorism Act 2000, Schedule 4 (further provision in relation to forfeiture orders)
dependencies.taken_as_input: nothing: what Schedule 4 provides is not encoded (a stated gap under the coverage row for s 23B(4))
